items.content:
중국 AI 기업들이 최첨단 모델의 성능을 확보하기 위해 집중적으로 분석하는 대상이 앤트로픽의 '클로드'에서 오픈AI의 'GPT-6 아스트라'로 바뀌고 있는 것으로 알려졌다. 딥시크와 문샷 AI는 최근 출시한 AI 모델을 개발하면서 아스트라의 출력 데이터를 학습에 상당 부분 활용한 것으로 전해졌다.

디 인포메이션은 28일(현지시간) 중국 AI 연구소들의 모델 개발에 정통한 관계자들을 인용, 앤트로픽이 자사 모델의 추론 정보를 빼내는 시도를 차단하자 중국 연구소들이 오픈AI 모델로 눈을 돌렸다고 보도했다.

문샷 AI는 지난주 공개한 '키미 K3.1 프로' 개발 과정에서 아스트라의 출력 결과를 활용했다고 사정을 잘 아는 관계자 3명이 밝혔다. 딥시크도 지난 17일 출시한 'V4.1-플래시-1017'의 성능 개선에 아스트라의 데이터를 활용했다고 다른 관계자 2명이 전했다.

두 회사가 사용한 방식은 '증류(Distillation)'로, 성능이 뛰어난 AI 모델의 응답이나 추론 결과를 학습 데이터로 활용해 다른 모델의 성능을 높이는 기술이다. 이를 활용하면 처음부터 모든 능력을 학습시키는 데 드는 시간과 비용을 줄일 수 있다.

이번에 아스트라가 주요 증류 대상으로 떠오른 데는 앤트로픽의 대응 강화가 영향을 미친 것으로 알려졌다. 중국 연구소들은 그동안 클로드 모델의 결과물을 집중적으로 수집해 왔지만, 최근 앤트로픽이 방어 체계를 강화하면서 데이터 확보가 어려워졌다는 것이다.

앤트로픽은 지난 12일 공식 블로그에서 새로운 방어 기술을 도입한 결과, 자체 평가에서 증류 공격자가 확보할 수 있는 데이터가 90~99% 줄었다고 밝혔다. 모델의 비공개 추론 과정을 외부로 추출하는 시도를 차단하고, 반복적으로 정보를 빼내려는 계정에는 사용 제한이나 정지 조치를 적용했다.

이처럼 클로드에서 유용한 학습 데이터를 확보하기 어려워지면서 중국 연구소들이 아스트라를 새로운 대상으로 선택했다는 설명이다.

오픈AI도 증류 시도를 차단하기 위해 대응을 강화하고 있다. 지난 9월 30일에는 공식 발표를 통해 문샷 AI 관련자들이 연루된 조직적인 모델 증류 공격을 적발했다고 밝혔다.

이에 따르면 공격자들은 지난 7월부터 대규모 계정을 이용해 모델의 비공개 추론 정보를 추출하려 했다. 오픈AI는 관련 활동을 차단했으며, 계정과 인프라에 대한 감시를 강화했다고 설명했다. 다만 이 사건은 아스트라 출시 이전에 발생한 것으로, 이번에 알려진 아스트라 증류 의혹과 동일한 사건은 아니다.

그럼에도 오픈AI 모델에서 학습 데이터를 추출하는 시도는 계속되고 있는 것으로 전해졌다. 중국 연구소들은 탐지를 피하기 위해 여러 계정을 사용하고 있으며, 유용한 데이터를 얻으려면 일반적인 사용보다 10배 이상 많은 프롬프트를 입력해야 하는 것으로 알려졌다.

오픈AI 대변인은 중국 연구소들의 증류 시도를 자세히 추적하고 있으며, 의심스러운 계정 차단과 사용 제한, 가입 통제 강화 등을 통해 대응하고 있다고 밝혔다. 또 "새로운 방어 체계를 구축하면 공격자들도 전술을 바꾸기 때문에 지속적인 개선이 필요하다"라고 설명했다.

중국 AI 기업들이 증류 기술에 의존하는 데는 미국의 첨단 AI 칩 수출 통제로 인한 컴퓨팅 자원 제약도 영향을 미친 것으로 분석된다. 중국 연구소들은 제한된 GPU 자원으로 미국의 최첨단 모델을 추격해야 하는 만큼, 기존 모델의 학습 결과를 활용하는 기술과 연산 효율 개선에 집중해 왔다.

실제로 딥시크는 제한된 컴퓨팅 자원으로 모델을 학습하는 기술을 발전시켜 왔으며, 문샷 AI와 Z.ai 등도 오픈웨이트 모델의 성능을 빠르게 개선하고 있다. 다만 중국 모델의 발전을 증류 기술만으로 설명할 수는 없으며, 자체적인 학습 알고리즘과 모델 구조 개선도 중요한 역할을 해 왔다.

특히 디 인포메이션은 딥시크의 모델 개발 과정을 아는 관계자들을 인용, 량원펑 CEO가 당초 차세대 V4 모델 개발에 증류 기술을 활용하는 데 부정적이었으나, Z.ai 등 경쟁사의 성과를 확인한 뒤 입장을 바꿨다고 전했다.

한편, 문샷 AI는 이번 아스트라 증류 의혹에 대한 논평을 거부했으며 딥시크는 논평 요청에 응답하지 않았다. 두 회사가 최신 모델 학습에 아스트라의 데이터를 얼마나 활용했는지에 대한 구체적인 규모와 방법도 공개되지 않았다.

items.title: A tiny world model running games on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/SheepSeb/tinyworldformer Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50295450 Points: 229 # Comments: 15
items.content:
Using 2 small neural networks to generate and play the game at the same time on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. The first one creates the game: given the current frame and the action, it predicts the next frame and the reward. The second one plays that game: it uses the generated frame and picks an action.

Every frame above was sampled by the world model network, and the actions were taken by the actor network.

I got interested in looped transformers, where one transformer block is applied several times with the same weights instead of stacking different layers. Reusing weights is cheap on memory, so I wanted to see if a looped world model could be small enough to run on a microcontroller. I picked the Pico 2 W because it is cheap and has an FPU, and small games because I could write the real versions directly into numpy and check every generated frame against them. Later I added a streaming RL agent so the board could also learn to play inside its own dream.

Contents: the two networks · the games · the world model · the agents · quantization · on the chip · flashing · browser · reproduce · code layout

The size depends on the game, some games require more parameters to learn them to be playable, we tried to get to keep the number of the parameters small enough.

On the chip neither network ever uses the real game: the actor only sees frames the world model, and the world model only gets actions from the actor. Both run on core 1 of the RP2350, while core 0 handles USB and the display.

The pretrained actor can be swapped for a fresh stream-x agent that learns from scratch on the board. And any button press hands control to you, so you can play the dream yourself.

Each game is a few hundred lines of numpy in src/tinyworldformer/games/ . It renders to a small grid of token ids, and one frame always holds the whole game state, so hidden state has to be drawn into the frame: the ball's heading is part of its token, and Doom-lite has a minimap.

"Exact frames" is the share of held-out transitions where every cell of the predicted frame matches the real game. Frames right after a random event are left out, since those can only be sampled, not predicted. Doom-lite's 3D view has 768 cells and a single shaded wall pixel off counts the whole frame as wrong, so its number looks worse than it plays; the game state is almost always right (see checking the dream ).

You can play the real games in a terminal: uv run python -m tinyworldformer.games.play --game pacman (or breakout , doomlite , flappy , pong ).

The frame is cut into square patches: 2×2 cells in Breakout, 4×4 in Doom-lite, Flappy Bird and Pong, 6×6 in Pac-Man. That gives 36 to 80 tokens per game. A patch's embedding is the sum of one learned vector per cell, with a separate table for each position inside the patch so the cell order isn't lost. Every token also gets a position vector and the action's vector.

The model is a single transformer block (attention plus a ReLU MLP) with one set of weights, applied 1 to 4 times, with the input added back before every pass. The output after every pass is trained against the next frame, so at run time the loop count trades speed for accuracy. On the Pico to keep a decent frame rate we use uses two loops.

The animation shows one held-out Doom-lite step. After one pass the model draws an enemy that isn't there, and each further pass removes part of it: 92, 35, 12, then 0 wrong cells. The bars on the right are the share of held-out frames each loop count gets exactly right.

Here is a dreamed Doom-lite step decoded after 1, 2, 3 and 4 loops, with red boxes on cells that differ from the real rules:

Exact held-out frames by loop count:

The model outputs a score for every cell and every token. Turning those scores into a frame turned out to matter almost as much as the model, and it ended up as three rules (shown above on Pong):

We implemented Rule 2 because the first Breakout model drew two balls at once; one global choice took exact frames from 91.6% to 99.7%.

Accuracy on recorded data wasn't enough. An agent drives the dream into states the data never had, and any mistake there is something it can exploit. So the main check runs while an agent plays: read the game state back off the dreamed frame ( games/<game>.py: read ), apply the real rules to that state and the agent's action, and compare the result with the next dreamed frame and reward.

5,000 dreamed steps per game at 2 loops, with the shipped agent ( training/evalwm.py --agent ):

First, agents play the real game and every step is recorded as one example (frame, action, next frame, reward), 1–3 million per game. Some episodes start from unusual states, like bricks with holes or random positions, so the data covers more of the game.

Then the world model learns to predict the next frame with a per-cell cross-entropy loss: 30k steps, with the first 3–4k steps run in float, then int8 rounding switches on ( QAT ).

The int8 weights are written into Rust source with every float stored as its exact bits. We check them with cargo test to reproduces the Python integer spec bit for bit, and then the firmware runs on the Pico.

An agent trained in the world model reaches states the recorded data never had, so record real games with that agent and fine-tune the world model on everything.

The agent in different games stated exploiting them so those are some fixes to it:

The agents use Stream AC(λ) (Elsayed, Vasan & Mahmood, 2024), which learns from one transition at a time: no replay buffer, no batches, no target network. Eligibility traces carry credit back in time, and ObGD shrinks any step that would overshoot the TD target. The policy and value networks each have two hidden layers of 64 units (32 on the Pico) with LayerNorm.

items.title: Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines
items.summary: The latest update also brings a cloud recovery option for PCs that won't boot.
items.content:
Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft’s quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs.

The preview update, KB5127936 , is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a “customize menu” button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the “Show more options” submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits.

The new preview also highlights a new Windows feature called Cloud Rebuild, a recovery option that can reinstall Windows 11 directly from the cloud, even when an existing Windows 11 fails to boot. Cloud Rebuild will pull the Windows 11 image and needed system drivers directly from Windows Update. Users will not need a custom recovery image or external media to reinstall Windows. There is an important distinction to note, however. Microsoft classifies Cloud Rebuild as a recovery option, but it behaves more like a fresh Windows install than a repair, as existing applications and files will not be included. Those worried about data security can sanitize entire system drives prior to reinstalling. For a full list of improvements coming to Windows 11, including changes to Xbox mode and settings, you can view the official Microsoft release announcement .

Microsoft’s latest quarterly report, released this week, paints a less encouraging picture of its Windows OEM business. “Windows OEM revenue was below expectations and decreased 27% and 28% in constant currency, driven by the Windows 10 end of support demand in the prior year, inventory drawdowns by OEM and channel partners and weaker PC market demand,” said CFO Amy Hood, according to a transcript of the call . The broader Windows OEM and devices category, which includes Microsoft’s own Surface lineup, fell 22 percent, per the earnings release. Hood went on to state that “we expect these trends to continue through the rest of the fiscal year.”

Recent hardware efforts like the Surface Laptop Ultra and broader RTX Spark platform arrived too late in the quarter to register in the results, and Microsoft forecast further drops before any possible boost from new hardware can show in its numbers. The news for Microsoft isn’t negative all around, though, as its Azure platform saw a 48 percent jump, and Microsoft Cloud revenue was also up 30 percent, year over year—now roughly 70 percent of the company’s $92.3 billion total quarterly revenue.

items.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
items.summary: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.
items.content:
Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its third-quarter earnings on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.”

The move is designed to protect its data from AI scraping, allowing the company to instead forge lucrative licensing deals with model providers. But just as important, such a shift could help Reddit to increase its revenue even as it faces daily active user declines in its largest market, the U.S.

Overall, Reddit’s global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in Q3 and were down 2% year-over-year.

The company is not alone in seeing such declines; the shift to an AI-centered web has impacted most websites and publishers by now, leading to fewer click-throughs, as AI summaries provide answers that don’t require website visits and Google’s traditional “ten blue links” have reduced relevance. (The change is now even impacting Google’s bottom line , its earnings revealed.)

But at Reddit’s scale, the numbers associated with such a decline are enormous. The comapny said search traffic referrals dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week in October. It warned that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low-double-digit percentage by next quarter. (To play that out: a hypothetical 10%–12% decline could bring Reddit to roughly 115 million–117 million daily actives, down from 130.3 million in Q3. That’s a huge drop!)

At the same time, Reddit has gotten significantly better at monetizing its audience even as its growth weakens. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of about $875 million. Net income rose 74% to $283 million. Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847 million while non-advertising revenue, which includes its AI data-licensing business, grew 35% year-over-year to $48 million.

And despite a 2% year-over-year decline in U.S. daily users, Reddit’s average revenue per daily active user in the U.S. rose 53% to $13.82. Globally, average revenue per daily active user increased 36% year-over-year to $6.87.

Shifting to a logged-in experience could boost those numbers even higher because logged-in users are typically worth more to advertisers.

Unlike the logged-out users who often find their way to the site via search, logged-in users provide more signals about their interests and behaviors, which helps to better target and personalize ads.

Still, a change of this magnitude could be the canary in the coalmine for the open web.

“I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me,” wrote Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman, in a post published on Reddit’s site . “But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business,” he said.

The company notes that the shift to the logged-in experience will not be an overnight change; it will first run tests in select markets outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. It doesn’t yet have a timeline for when the change will be rolled out to all its users worldwide. It also acknowledged that access to a logged-out front page is important.

Plus, Reddit pointed out that being logged in doesn’t mean having to give up anonymity, nor will it remove its option to browse anonymously through its “incognito mode” experience, which is being rebuilt.

There are still plenty of questions that are unanswered, particularly around where the boundaries should be between logged-in and logged-out experiences,” Hoffman wrote. “This is a big evolution for Reddit, and not one we’re taking lightly. But I believe it’s the right next step for the platform and for our future.”

items.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant
items.summary: Rivian doesn't disclose if the value of its $5.8 billion joint venture will expand as a result.
items.content:
The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants.

Rivian is now licensing elements of its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group as part of the broader joint venture, according to the company’s third-quarter investor presentation released Thursday.

Rivian didn’t disclose the licensing fees, payment terms, or which Volkswagen vehicles will use the technology. However, the AI assistant, which recently rolled out to Rivian vehicles , could make its Volkswagen debut in the automaker’s low-cost EV called the ID EVERY1 . The small four-door hatchback is slated to be the first VW vehicle to use Rivian’s software and electrical architecture under the joint venture established in 2024.

The joint venture between Rivian and VW Group has already expanded once before, at least financially. The companies initially announced a joint venture valued up to $5 billion , but within months VW upped its commitment to invest up to $5.8 billion in Rivian by 2027. The initial tie-up, formalized through an independent company that kicked off in November 2024, focused on bringing Rivian’s electrical architecture and software to Volkswagen’s next-generation of vehicles.

Rivian described the expansion to include elements of its AI assistant technology as “a proof point for the extensibility of the platform we’ve built in-house.”

Rivian spent two years developing its AI assistant before showing it off last year. That development work continued longer than expected, with the assistant finally rolling out in September 2026 to its flagship R1S SUV, R1T pickup truck, and new midsize R2 SUV.

Rivian has big aspirations for its AI assistant, which allows drivers and passengers to interact with the vehicle and control certain functions. Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe told TechCrunch onstage at Disrupt 2026 that the company has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. That capability could eventually allow Rivian vehicles to run AI agents created by other companies, including Anthropic.

The in-house AI assistant program also fits into Rivian’s push to become more vertically integrated — a strategy the company emphasized in its third-quarter earnings report.

“Our relentless focus on vertical integration remains a core competitive differentiator, allowing Rivian to seamlessly unify our hardware and software architecture to deliver significant value to our customers,” the company noted in its investor presentation.

That strategy led to Rivian overhauling its flagship R1T truck and R1S SUV , changing everything from the battery pack and suspension system to the electrical architecture, sensor stack, and software user interface. Its new electric architecture system and compute platform slashed the amount of wiring used and reduced the total number of electronic control units, or computers, used to control the vehicle from 17 different ECUs to seven. That foundation, Rivian argued, would allow it to build vehicles that can handle the computing demands required for advanced software and automated driving.

That technology caught the attention (and money) of VW, which has struggled to offer customers a modern software-centric vehicle found in competitors like Tesla.

Rivian made that vertical-integration case repeatedly in its investor presentation, noting that because it controls the entire technology stack, including compute, sensors, displays, lighting and sound, “it can roll out rapid, vehicle-wide OTA updates that go well beyond the basics. “

items.title: Trump declares robot imports a national security threat
items.summary: President orders trade talks on foreign-made factory robots, threatens tariffs.
items.content:
President Donald Trump has declared the imports of foreign-made factory robots to be a national security threat—ordering new US negotiations with trading partners while holding out the possibility of imposing new tariffs on such robot imports in the future.

Issued on October 28, Trump’s presidential proclamation represents heightened government scrutiny of foreign-made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major US corporations that rely on such robots. Those companies include Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla , and aerospace and defense giants like Boeing and Lockheed Martin.

Trump’s proclamation describes industrial robots and machinery as being crucial for producing US military weapon systems along with representing a “driving force” behind all critical infrastructure sectors within the US economy. The proclamation cites an investigation under US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick as having found that US imports of such robots “pose[] risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long-term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.”

The Department of Commerce investigation also supposedly found “unique security and safety risks” that may introduce “significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities that can result in severe consequences to the United States.”

Such wording echoes justifications used by Trump’s Federal Communications Commission when it banned new models of foreign-made robots, such as robotic vacuums, four-legged robot dogs, and humanoid robots, in July 2026. But that FCC action had specifically exempted industrial robot arms and other fixed or stationary robots commonly deployed in automotive factories and logistics warehouses.

Now Trump’s directive for the United States and trading partners “to adjust imports of robotics, industrial machinery, and their components” aims to strike new agreements on the issue within 180 days of the proclamation’s date. If no agreements have been reached by then, the proclamation warns that the president may take additional actions, like imposing “tariffs, duties, quotas, and fees” on such imports.

Any tariffs or other fees would, of course, be paid by the US companies importing such foreign-made robots. That would likely increase the cost of US manufacturing operations at a time when the United States has become the second largest market in using industrial robots, with the International Federation of Robotics reporting nearly 38,500 new US installations of industrial robots in 2025.

Major US automotive and aerospace companies often buy large robotic arms for factory floor work from the “big four” robotics makers—FANUC, ABB, Yaskawa, and KUKA—that are headquartered in Japan, Switzerland, and Germany. No US company currently offers comparable heavy-duty hardware for large industrial robotic arms, although the foreign robotics makers have been expanding their US engineering and assembly facilities.

Even Amazon, the company that has arguably deployed more robot workers than any other in the world, still uses some foreign-made robots, like Japan’s FANUC robotic arms, despite having significantly ramped up its own in-house robot production and developed certain specialized robotic arms.

Trump’s own proclamation acknowledges that US robotics companies do not produce enough industrial robots to “meet national security needs,” and that the United States “relies on foreign imports for most types of robotics and industrial machinery and for their components.”

If Trump eventually slaps tariffs on US imports of foreign-made industrial robots, that would at least fall short of restricting imports outright. Although as Intel recently showed, major US companies can still get waivers from the Trump administration to continue using foreign-made robots even when a nominal ban is in place.

items.content:
Editing files you generate with Gemini no longer requires leaving the app.﻿

Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini . The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now.

Google added support for generating and downloading files in Gemini earlier this year, but now you can tweak those files without leaving the Gemini app. Google says you can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text in files to ask Gemini questions or prompt it to make changes to the file, like highlighting a table and asking Gemini to turn it into a graph.

You could already use Gemini to edit files with its integrations in Google’s Workspace apps, like the Gemini bar in Google Docs . Anthropic also launched a feature earlier this year that allows users to generate and edit documents and presentations in Claude chats.

items.title: Trump ignored intel on China’s Nvidia spy to protect company’s stock, report says
items.summary: Spy accused of exploiting Trump ties to Huang, funneling secrets to China.
items.content:
Donald Trump apparently is so aligned with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—who has become the president’s key advisor on AI —that he ignored intelligence indicating that Huang was the target of a “Chinese spy plot,” and did so partly to protect Nvidia’s stock.

The New York Times spoke with people briefed on US intelligence agencies’ surveillance and granted them anonymity to discuss findings drawn from “classified intelligence.” According to sources, about a year ago, Trump was briefed that “Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access” to Huang. That “someone” was Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and former top executive at a Singapore cloud company called Megaspeed.

According to sources, the US had already suspected that Alice Huang—who is not related to Jensen Huang—was helping China evade export controls to gain access to high-end Nvidia chips through Megaspeed. But it alarmed investigators to discover that she may have used her role at Megaspeed to gain direct access to Jensen Huang. It’s now believed she may have leveraged that closeness to feed China intel not only on one of America’s leading AI companies, but also to influence Trump’s thinking on AI. As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted last month ahead of Trump’s AI talks with China President Xi Jinping, “the president is completely aligned with Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia.”

At least partly due to fears that US action against the alleged spying could hobble Nvidia chip sales or disrupt the delicate US-China trade truce, Trump “chose not to do anything with the information,” sources said.

Soon after US scrutiny increased, Alice Huang’s name was removed from Megaspeed corporate documents. At this stage, it’s unclear “how closely she is still connected to Megaspeed,” NYT reported.

Liu Chang, the spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, told NYT that the US accusations against Alice Huang are baseless. He accused the US of pursuing a campaign of “groundless smears and slanders” against China.

It’s not clear which agencies were investigating Alice Huang or what triggered their suspicions, NYT reported. Sources also could not explain what information she may have shared with Beijing.

Nvidia has denied that she would have had access to any trade secrets, but it seems notable that Jensen Huang did not receive a defensive briefing that Americans sometimes get when they’re targets of foreign spying. Some senior officials think it’s unlikely that Jensen Huang would have “remained unaware” of Alice Huang’s alleged intelligence-gathering for the entire duration of their professional relationship, although Trump was told Jensen Huang had no knowledge at the time of his briefing. It seems possible that Jensen Huang got no briefing because US agencies worried that he might tip her off that “she was being watched,” the NYT reported.

Trump’s deep ties with tech leaders have been criticized throughout his administration, but Jensen Huang’s influence increasingly stands out . To critics, the political friendship appears to be largely based on growing his business in China. Since cozying up to Trump, the Nvidia CEO has gotten export controls relaxed and even struck a controversial deal giving the US a 25 percent cut of some chip sales so he could try to sell more chips in China. Sources told NYT that “some investigations and proposed trade sanctions involving China or Nvidia” have “ground to a halt within the Commerce Department” due to Jensen Huang’s influence.

No one’s sure when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, but NYT found social media photos that predated her role arranging a Megaspeed purchase of $2 billion in chips over the next year. If those chips ended up in China, the US worried they “could help adversaries like China develop new weapons, surveil dissidents, and leap ahead of the United States in AI development,” NYT reported. To US agencies, it’s particularly concerning that Megaspeed may be doing China’s bidding by supplying chips to giant data centers in Malaysia and Indonesia “that appear to remotely serve customers in China,” NYT reported earlier this month.

Sources told the NYT that US intelligence agencies conducted electronic surveillance of Alice Huang and found that “she was in contact with an American citizen.” Since agencies could not legally surveil the American citizen without a court order, they sought to unmask the citizen by showing a “need for information.”

“In this case, the unmasking process identified Mr. Huang as the US citizen,” NYT reported.

Megaspeed is an Nvidia customer, and Nvidia has independently investigated whether Megaspeed is funneling its chips to China. That investigation concluded that there were no signs of diversion and that Megaspeed has raised no red flags as a customer, Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told NYT.

Both Nvidia and Megaspeed insist that the cloud company has Singapore-based owners, but NYT visited the supposed offices and talked to anyone they could find to probe the actual business operations. Among red flags raised, NYT noted that staffers suggested “it’s not clear” what Megaspeed as a company does and confirmed that the Singapore director, James Tan, lives in China and is “never present.” (NYT’s review of corporate ownership documents showed Tan owns the shell company that owns Megaspeed.)

In that story published earlier this month, NYT detailed how Alice Huang was seemingly growing increasingly close to Jensen Huang, citing several photos of them together. That includes a photo at an event where she reportedly bragged, “I bet you guys I can get Jensen here,” and then he arrived in his trademark leather jacket to take whiskey shots.

Rizzo said that it was common for Nvidia’s CEO to attend parties with customers and partners, where he discussed “updates on the market.” One source told NYT that Jensen Huang had always planned to attend that party.

items.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
items.summary: Google's negative cash flow balloons to -$9.06 billion, and stock price tumbles following Q3 earnings.
items.content:
Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company’s stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history. It comes down to several troubling aspects of the new report, including an admission by the company that AI search isn’t earning as much as organic search, and despite that, Google expects to spend even more on AI next year.

The company took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, earning more than $26 billion in net income. These may sound like good numbers, but financial markets are not impressed. While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower. As of this story’s publication, the stock price is down almost 12 percent, and it was down about 13 percent earlier in the day.

While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more. Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02. Google’s Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue. That’s about a billion more than analyst guesses.

During the earnings call, Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler discussed the company’s search volume. This is one of the key metrics by which Google tracks its own performance. In the last quarter, Google saw search grow by 12 percent versus last year. Good for the company, right? Except that’s a much slower rate than previous quarters. Growth in Q2 was 17 percent, and Q1 saw 19 percent growth over 2025. Search revenue was also flat in Q3.

So that’s the first problem, likely driven by more consumers using AI chatbots to find answers. The other issue is that Google’s take on AI search isn’t pulling in revenue like standard web search yet. According to Schindler, each AI Mode query earns less revenue compared to a similar web search—there are fewer ads, and they cost less to run.

While Schindler suggested AI mode revenue was set to increase, he was also careful to control expectations. Advertisers may need time, he said, to understand the value in AI search ads. The company’s research reportedly shows that users find these ads more relevant and helpful than the ones they see in traditional search.

As part of the financial disclosure, Google announced an expansion of ads in AI Mode. If you do decide to dip into Google’s search chatbot, you’ll probably see more contextual advertising. These ads will begin appearing in more international markets soon. In the US, where AI Mode ads were already becoming commonplace, Google will implement multi-turn ads. That means the sponsored links will change continuously as you engage in a back-and-forth with the robot. CEO Sundar Pichai noted that these complex interactions are becoming more common as Google pushes more users toward AI Mode.

Google is not slowing down—it’s only going to accelerate the shift toward more AI. Like last quarter , Google reported negative cash flow in Q3. The loss actually increased from -$5.8 billion to -$9.06 billion, a situation that is directly attributable to Google’s runaway AI spending. Google had capital expenditures of $51.4 billion in Q3 and says it still expects total 2026 spending to be between $195 billion and $205 billion. In 2027, Google is targeting more than $300 billion of AI investment.

Credit: Google Credit: Google

To support this continued spending, Google points to its cloud revenue more than doubling over the past year. It’s easy to see why the company is so keen to keep expanding in AI based on that. The company’s AI compute infrastructure doesn’t just power Gemini. Countless AI startups pay to run models on Google’s infrastructure. But even the larger AI firms are using venture cash to do it, and if that funding were to dry up, Google’s cloud revenues could go with it.

While Google’s investments ensure it still turns a profit, the trend of spending more than it earns on products and services (that negative cash flow) could come back to bite it. Search growth is declining, and Google is placing all its eggs in the AI basket. If spending on cloud services in the industry drops or search growth stalls, the company could be looking at a lot more red in its future.

items.title: H.264 Is Magic (2016)
items.summary: Article URL: https://sidbala.com/h-264-is-magic/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50291054 Points: 450 # Comments: 151
items.content:
H.264 is a video compression codec standard. It is ubiquitous - internet video, Blu-ray, phones, security cameras, drones, everything. Everything uses H.264 now.

H.264 is a remarkable piece of technology. It is the result of 30+ years of work with one single goal: To reduce the bandwidth required for transmission of full-motion video.

Technically, it is very interesting. This post will give insight into some of the details at a high level - I hope to not bore you too much with the intricacies. Also note that many of the concepts explained here apply to video compression in general, and not just H.264.

Why even compress anything?

A simple uncompressed video file will contain an array of 2D buffers containing pixel data for each frame. So it's a 3D (2 spatial dimensions and 1 temporal) array of bytes. Each pixel takes 3 bytes to store - one byte each for the three primary colors (red, green and blue).

1080p @ 60 Hz = 1920x1080x60x3 => ~ 370 MB/sec of raw data.

This is next to impossible to deal with. A 50GB Blu-ray disk will only hold ~2 mins. You can't move it anywhere fast. Even SSDs have trouble dumping this straight from RAM to Disk[^1].

So yeah. We need compression.

Why H.264 compression?

Yes, I will answer this. But first let me show you something. Here is the Apple Homepage:

I captured the screen of this home page and produced two files:

Eh. What? Those file sizes look switched.

No, they're right. The H.264 video, 300 frames long is 175KB. A single frame of that video in PNG is 1015KB.

It looks like we're storing 300 times the amount of data in the video. But the file size is a fifth. So H.264 would seem to be 1500x as efficient as PNG.

How is this even possible? All right, what's the trick?

There are very many tricks! H.264 uses all the tricks you can think of (and tons you can't think of). Let's go through the important ones.

Imagine you're building a car for street racing. You need to go faster. What is the first thing you do? You shed some weight. Your car weighs 3000 lbs. You throw away stuff you don't need. Those back seats? pfft. Chuck those. That subwoofer? Gone. No music for you. Air Conditioning? Yeah, ditch it. Transmission? Ye..no. Wait! We're gonna need that.

You remove everything except the things that matter.

This concept of throwing away bits you don't need to save space is called lossy compression. H.264 is a lossy codec - it throws away less important bits and only keeps the important bits.

PNG is a lossless codec. It means that nothing is thrown away. Bit for bit, the original source image can be recovered from a PNG encoded image.

Important bits? How does the algorithm know what bits in my frame are important?

There are few obvious ways to trim out images. Maybe the top right quadrant is useless all the time. So maybe we can zero out those pixels and discard that quadrant. We would use only 3/4th of the space we need. ~2200 lbs now. Or maybe we can crop out a thick border around the edges of the frame, the important stuff is in the middle anyway. Yes, you could do these. But H.264 doesn't do this.

What does H.264 actually do?

H.264, like other lossy image algorithms, discards detail information. Here is a close-up of the original compared with the image post-discard.

See how the compressed one does not show the holes in the speaker grills in the MacBook Pro? If you don't zoom in, you would even notice the difference. The image on the right weighs in at 7% the size of the original - and we haven't even compressed the image in the traditional sense. Imagine your car weighed just 200 lbs!

7% wow! How do you discard detail information like that?

For this we need a quick math lesson.

Now we're getting to the juicy bits! Ha puns! If you took an information theory class, you might remember information entropy. Information entropy is the number of bits required to represent some information. Note that it is not simply the size of some dataset. It is minimum number of bits that must be used to represent all the information contained in a dataset.

For example, if your dataset is the result of a single coin toss, you need 1 bit of entropy. If you have record two coin tosses, you'll need 2 bits. Makes sense?

Suppose you have some strange coin - you've tossed it 10 times, and every time it lands on heads. How would you describe this information to someone? You wouldn't say HHHHHHHHH. You would just say "10 tosses, all heads" - bam! You've just compressed some data! Easy. I saved you hours of mindfuck lectures. This is obviously an oversimplification, but you've transformed some data into another shorter representation of the same information. You've reduced data redundancy . The information entropy in this dataset has not changed - you've just converted between representations.
